title: Sitting versus standing and Barnes's neck problem from the palace stage
summary: Barnes says old bands rarely stood, and recalls a neck problem from always looking up while playing in the pit at the palace.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, I think of it. What about sitting down and standing up? In the old days, did they stand up sometimes when they take a chorus or the whole band stand up much? Or did they always sit down?
Oh, they take a very few chorus we had.
Yeah, that's true, I know too.

The only chorus we had was we had something in Scotty music. Yeah. That the man had, but he didn't stand up. He had to. He stands up if he wanted or any other way or sit down. See, now, many men stand up in a manner because they got more of that sitting up. It's better than sitting down in the clinic. You see this one here? Yeah, yeah. You know what that is? That's them sitting down here and watching them show up there. Oh, yeah?
I was playing in the palace here. Oh.
Sitting down playing and watching them up there. See, when they jump their mates, we had to be with them. You had to watch them and that's where I got back here. Well, what buddies are they?
They're sort of a muscle? Well, I didn't know.
I went to the doctor to this and he said there's nothing to it. Nothing to it.

Trying to give you a cricket, your neck here sort of thing. Yeah. No, he said, after the war, I mean, I could have it removed, but I didn't know what's there. But in the meantime, that's what I got. Yeah, yeah. I was sitting and waiting on the palace, playing, and looking up. You see? Always looking up like that, playing with you, you know, couldn't hold the plan and looking up like that. You had to get on some. You moved your head. Yeah. And by doing that, that's what I got.
